meta.title: Individual deductions
meta.summary: Deductions for AGI, the new senior and car loan deductions, itemized deductions for medical costs, taxes, interest and charity, and the choice between itemizing and the standard deduction.

videos.title: Deductions for AGI
videos.take: Above-the-line deductions include half of SE tax, HSA and IRA contributions, and student loan interest

scenes.say: Above-the-line deductions are the best kind: everyone who qualifies gets them, and they lower AGI. Here are the main ones.

scenes.heading: Common deductions for AGI
scenes.say: The main deductions for AGI are half of self-employment tax, health insurance premiums for the self-employed, contributions to traditional IRAs and self-employed retirement plans, contributions to a health savings account, and up to $2,500 of student loan interest.

scenes.heading: 2026 contribution limits
scenes.say: For 2026 the IRA limit is $7,500, plus $1,100 if you're fifty or older. Health savings account limits are $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage.
Why half of self-employment tax? Employers deduct their half of payroll tax as a business expense. Letting the self-employed deduct half puts them on a similar footing.

scenes.heading: Nora's deductions for AGI
scenes.say: Suppose Nora also puts $3,000 into a family health savings account. With half her self-employment tax, that's $5,119 of deductions for AGI, saving $614 of income tax at twelve percent.

scenes.q: Which is a deduction for AGI?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which is a deduction for AGI? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C. Student loan interest is above the line. The others are itemized deductions.

videos.title: New deductions: seniors and car loans
videos.take: From 2025 to 2028, seniors deduct up to $6,000 and buyers of new US-assembled cars deduct up to $10,000 of loan interest

scenes.say: The 2025 tax law created new deductions you can take whether or not you itemize. Two of them: one for seniors and one for car loans.

sub: Up to $6,000 per person 65 or older,
scenes.say: Each taxpayer aged sixty-five or older can deduct up to $6,000 from 2025 through 2028, on top of the standard or itemized deductions. It phases out by six percent of modified AGI above $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return.

scenes.heading: Gary, single, 67
scenes.say: Gary, single and sixty-seven, has AGI of $23,500. His standard deduction with the over-sixty-five amount is $18,150. The $6,000 senior deduction takes his taxable income to zero.

sub: Up to $10,000 a year, new personal vehicle
with final assembly in the US
scenes.say: The second: interest on a loan for a new personal car, truck or SUV whose final assembly was in the United States. Up to $10,000 a year is deductible from 2025 through 2028, phasing out above $100,000 of modified AGI, or $200,000 joint.

scenes.heading: Jake's new US-built pickup
scenes.say: Jake buys a new, US-assembled pickup for personal use and pays $1,800 of loan interest in 2026. The Lindqvists are well under the $200,000 threshold, so they deduct it all, saving $216.

scenes.q: Which car loan qualifies for the deduction?
opts: A new US-assembled car for personal use
A new imported car assembled in Japan
A new delivery van used only in Nora's business
scenes.say: Quick check. Which car loan qualifies for the new deduction? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The vehicle must be new, for personal use, with final assembly in the US. Business vehicle interest is deducted as a business expense instead.

videos.title: Itemized deductions: medical expenses
videos.take: Unreimbursed medical expenses are deductible only above 7.5% of AGI

scenes.say: Itemized deductions start with medical expenses. They're deductible, but only after a big floor.

scenes.heading: Qualifying medical expenses
items: Health insurance premiums you pay after tax
scenes.say: Qualifying costs include payments to doctors, dentists and hospitals, prescription drugs, health insurance premiums you pay with after-tax dollars, and travel for medical care.

scenes.big: Only the part above 7.5% of AGI
sub: Less any insurance or HSA reimbursement
scenes.say: Only unreimbursed expenses above seven point five percent of AGI are deductible. Anything paid by insurance or from a health savings account doesn't count.

scenes.heading: The Lindqvists' medical deduction
scenes.say: If the Lindqvists paid $10,000 of unreimbursed medical costs, the floor is seven point five percent of $116,281, or $8,721. Only $1,279 is deductible, and only if they itemize.

sub: Schedule elective care into one year
scenes.say: That's why timing matters. Scheduling elective procedures in the same year can push costs over the floor.

scenes.q: AGI is $60,000 and unreimbursed medical costs are $5,000. What is deductible?
scenes.say: Quick check. AGI is sixty thousand dollars and unreimbursed medical costs are five thousand. What's deductible? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The floor is $4,500, so $500 is deductible.

videos.title: Itemized deductions: taxes and the SALT cap
videos.take: State and local taxes are deductible up to $40,400 in 2026, less for very high incomes

scenes.say: State and local taxes, or SALT, are deductible. But there's a cap, and it changed in 2025.

scenes.heading: Deductible taxes
items: State and local income tax, or sales tax instead
Personal property tax based on value
scenes.say: You can deduct state and local income taxes, or sales taxes instead if you choose, plus real estate taxes and personal property taxes based on value.

scenes.heading: The SALT cap
scenes.say: From 2018 to 2024, the deduction was capped at $10,000. The 2025 law raised it to $40,000 for 2025 and $40,400 for 2026, rising one percent a year, before returning to $10,000 in 2030.

sub: Cap falls by 30% of the excess,
scenes.say: For 2026 the cap shrinks by thirty percent of modified AGI above $505,000, but never below $10,000.

scenes.heading: The Lindqvists' taxes
scenes.say: The Lindqvists paid $5,500 of Minnesota income tax and $3,200 of property tax. That's $8,700, well under the cap.

scenes.q: A couple with MAGI of $555,000 paid $45,000 of state taxes in 2026. What is their SALT cap?
scenes.say: Quick check. A couple with modified AGI of five hundred fifty-five thousand dollars paid forty-five thousand of state taxes. What's their SALT cap? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. They're $50,000 over the threshold. Thirty percent of that is $15,000, and $40,400 minus $15,000 is $25,400.

videos.title: Itemized deductions: interest and charity
videos.take: Home mortgage interest on up to $750,000 of debt and gifts to charity are itemized deductions; from 2026, non-itemizers deduct cash gifts too

scenes.say: The other big itemized deductions are mortgage interest and gifts to charity, and charity changed in 2026.

sub: Interest on up to $750,000 of debt
to buy, build or improve your home
scenes.say: Mortgage interest is deductible on up to $750,000 of debt used to buy, build or substantially improve your main home and one other home. From 2026, mortgage insurance premiums count as interest again.

scenes.heading: Charitable gifts
items: To qualified charities only, not people
Appreciated property: fair value, up to 30%
A receipt for any gift of $250 or more
scenes.say: Gifts to qualified charities are deductible; gifts to individuals aren't. Cash gifts are limited to sixty percent of AGI, appreciated long-term property is deducted at fair value up to thirty percent, and any single gift of $250 or more needs a written acknowledgment.

scenes.heading: Charity from 2026
scenes.say: From 2026, itemizers can deduct only the part of their gifts above half a percent of AGI. And non-itemizers get a new deduction for cash gifts: up to $1,000, or $2,000 on a joint return, on top of the standard deduction.

scenes.heading: Maria gives $1,500 to her church
scenes.say: Maria Ortiz takes the head of household standard deduction and gives $1,500 to her church. As a non-itemizer filing alone, she can deduct $1,000, saving $120.

opts: $500 to a neighbor whose house burned down
Ten hours of volunteer work worth $300
scenes.say: Quick check. Which gift is deductible? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Gifts must go to a qualified charity. Gifts to individuals and political campaigns aren't deductible, and the value of your time never is.

videos.title: Standard deduction or itemize?
videos.take: Itemize only if itemized deductions exceed the standard deduction; most families now take the standard deduction

scenes.say: Every year, every taxpayer takes the larger of the standard deduction or their itemized deductions. Let's run the Lindqvists' numbers.

scenes.heading: The Lindqvists' itemized deductions
scenes.say: The Lindqvists' $3,000 of medical costs is below the floor. Taxes are $8,700 and mortgage interest is $9,800. That's $18,500 of itemized deductions, far less than the $32,200 standard deduction.
So they take the standard deduction. Since the 2017 law nearly doubled it, about nine out of ten filers do the same.

sub: Pile two years of deductions into one,
scenes.say: Families near the line can bunch: pay two years of charitable gifts, or schedule medical care, in one year to itemize, then take the standard deduction the next.

scenes.heading: Deductions everyone keeps
items: Senior, tips, overtime and car loan deductions
scenes.say: And remember what you keep either way: the deductions for AGI, the business income deduction, the new senior, tips, overtime and car loan deductions, and from 2026, the charitable deduction for non-itemizers.

scenes.q: A single filer has $9,000 of state taxes, $6,000 of mortgage interest and $2,000 of gifts (AGI $100,000). Itemize?
opts: No: itemizing is only for couples
scenes.say: Quick check. A single filer has nine thousand dollars of state taxes, six thousand of mortgage interest and two thousand of gifts, with AGI of a hundred thousand. Should she itemize? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Half a percent of $100,000 is $500, so $1,500 of the gifts count. $9,000 plus $6,000 plus $1,500 is $16,500, just above $16,100.

warmup: Which personal expenses do you think should be deductible: rent, student loan interest, medical bills, gifts to church, car payments? Vote, then we'll see what the law says.
Collect votes. Reveal: student loan interest (above the line), medical (over 7.5%), charity (yes), car loan interest (only new US-assembled cars, 2025–2028), rent (no). Leads to 6.1 and 6.2.
acts: Nora, 37, has family HDHP cover. What is the most she and Jake can put into an HSA for 2026, and what does it save at 12% income tax?
$8,750 family limit; saves $1,050 of income tax (more if contributed through payroll, avoiding FICA).
A married couple, both 66, have MAGI of $170,000. What is their total senior deduction?
AGI $80,000; medical costs: doctor $2,500, prescriptions $1,200, gym membership $600, health premiums paid after tax $4,000, insurance reimbursed $1,000 of the doctor bills. Deductible amount?
A single filer with MAGI of $600,000 paid $50,000 of state income and property tax in 2026. What can she deduct?
The Lindqvists give $1,800 cash to their church in 2026 and take the standard deduction. What can they deduct? What if they itemized?
Non-itemizer: up to $2,000 joint, so $1,800. If itemizing: only the amount over 0.5% × 116,281 = 581, i.e. $1,219.
How could the Lindqvists bunch to itemize? Estimate what they'd need.
Itemized $18,500 vs $32,200: they'd need about $13,700 more, e.g. several years' charitable gifts through a donor-advised fund in one year. Probably not worth it.
case: Erik and Kari Lindqvist live in Minneapolis and file jointly. Their 2026 AGI is $280,000. They paid $14,000 of Minnesota income tax and $9,500 of property tax, $16,000 of interest on a $500,000 mortgage, $3,000 of unreimbursed medical costs, and gave $6,000 cash to charity. They also contributed $8,750 to an HSA through Kari's employer.
What is the value of itemizing at their marginal rate?
How does the HSA affect the calculation?

Taxes 23,500 (under $40,400); mortgage interest 16,000 (debt under $750,000); medical 0 (floor 21,000); charity 6,000 − 0.5% × 280,000 = 4,600. Total $44,100 vs $32,200: itemize, $11,900 more. Taxable income about $235,900 puts them in the 24% bracket, so itemizing is worth about $2,856. The HSA contribution through payroll is excluded from wages, so it already reduced AGI (and payroll tax).
exam: Distinguish deductions for AGI from itemized deductions and explain why the distinction matters. Give two examples of each.

For AGI: available to all, reduce AGI (e.g. half SE tax, HSA, IRA, student loan interest). Itemized: only if they exceed the standard deduction (medical over 7.5%, SALT up to cap, mortgage interest, charity). AGI drives floors and phase-outs.

A single taxpayer, AGI $90,000, has medical costs of $8,000, state taxes of $7,000, mortgage interest of $5,500 and cash gifts to charity of $1,450. Compute itemized deductions and advise whether to itemize in 2026.
Medical 8,000 − 6,750 = 1,250; taxes 7,000; interest 5,500; charity 1,450 − 450 = 1,000. Total 14,750 < 16,100: take the standard deduction plus $1,000 non-itemizer charitable deduction.
outcomes: Apply the senior and car loan deductions
Deduct mortgage interest and charitable gifts
Choose between itemizing and the standard deduction
take: Above-the-line deductions help everyone and lower AGI
Seniors get $6,000 and new-car buyers up to $10,000, through 2028
Medical costs count only above 7.5% of AGI
Mortgage interest up to $750,000 of debt; charity has a 0.5% floor and a non-itemizer deduction
Take the larger of standard or itemized

ex.why: Above-the-line deductions reduce AGI; itemized deductions compete with the standard deduction.

ex.q: A single filer, 70, has MAGI of $85,000. What is her senior deduction for 2026?
AGI is $70,000 and unreimbursed medical costs are $9,000. What is the medical deduction?
A couple with MAGI of $305,000 paid $48,000 of state and local taxes in 2026. How much can they deduct?
ex.why: MAGI is under $505,000, so the full $40,400 cap applies.

ex.q: From 2026, how much can a married couple who take the standard deduction deduct for $3,000 of cash gifts to charity?
ex.why: Non-itemizers can deduct cash gifts up to $2,000 on a joint return.

ex.q: An itemizer with AGI of $120,000 gives $5,000 cash to charity in 2026. How much is deductible?
ex.why: Only gifts above 0.5% of AGI (600) count: 5,000 − 600 = 4,400.

ex.q: Which mortgage interest is deductible as qualified residence interest?
opts: Interest on a home equity loan used to buy a boat
Interest on a $600,000 loan to buy a main home
Interest on a loan for a rental property
Interest on a credit card used for furniture
ex.why: Acquisition debt up to $750,000 on a main or second home qualifies; equity debt must be used to buy, build or improve the home.

ex.q: A married couple's itemized deductions total $29,000. What deduction do they take?
ex.why: Take the larger: the $32,200 standard deduction.
